items.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] When Bill Haley and Elvis came on the scene, you would have been about 9 or 10. So that makes sense. [INTERVIEWEE] That’s about right, yeah

ctx.x: Rock-and-roll. I loved – I don’t know if I heard Rock Around the Clock when it came out, but I was there certainly pretty close to the beginning. And Elvis was my big hero, Elvis Presley. Even I used to sing, when I was on crutches – because I had the polio thing, which I’m sure we’ll get to eventually – I would take the crutch, like a guitar, stand in front of the mirror, and think I was Elvis. I sang Hound Dog, Don’t Be Cruel, Heartbreak Hotel. I loved Elvis Presley. So I was – the first musical experience,…
When Bill Haley and Elvis came on the scene, you would have been about 9 or 10. So that makes sense.

That’s about right, yeah And I loved – to get to it, I liked the sound of the saxophone. And of course since early rock-and-roll, as you know, had – the saxophone was the main soloing instrument, 8 bars here and there. I liked the tenor. I didn’t even – certainly didn’t know what it was. Nobody in my immediate family – I never saw a tenor. But I liked the sound of it, and I wanted to play that instrument from rock-and-roll, right from the beginning.
